key.name: tv-shows-path
key.description: Superseded by tv-shows-folders; read only while that list is empty. One subfolder per show, optionally split into Season N subfolders.

key.name: tv-shows-folders
key.description: One subfolder per show, optionally split into Season N subfolders. Tried in order; a show that appears in two folders is listed twice.

key.name: tv-shows-sources
key.description: Tried in order until one answers. An entry is a provider, optionally with a credential slot ("tmdb@2"); a slot with no credential is skipped.

key.name: tv-shows-online
key.summary: Fetch artwork and descriptions online for TV shows
key.description: Off leaves this section with whatever is already cached. Every section has its own; there is no longer a global switch.

key.name: tv-shows-open-command
key.description: Command this section's files open with; the file's path is appended. The default plays in VLC full screen and closes it when the file ends, with VLC's own "continue playback" off, since resume-playback does that. Empty uses the system default application, and so does a command that is not installed.

key.name: films-path
key.description: Superseded by films-folders; read only while that list is empty. One subfolder or file per film, named "Title (Year)".

key.name: films-folders
key.description: One subfolder or file per film, named "Title (Year)".

key.name: films-sources
key.description: Tried in order until one answers. TMDB with no key set is skipped, which leaves Wikipedia.

key.name: films-online
key.summary: Fetch artwork and descriptions online for films
key.description: Off leaves this section with whatever is already cached. Every section has its own; there is no longer a global switch.

key.name: films-open-command
key.description: Command this section's files open with; the file's path is appended. The default plays in VLC full screen and closes it when the file ends, with VLC's own "continue playback" off, since resume-playback does that. Empty uses the system default application, and so does a command that is not installed.

key.name: music-path
key.description: Superseded by music-folders; read only while that list is empty. Album folders, optionally grouped under artist folders.

key.name: music-folders
key.description: Album folders, optionally grouped under artist folders. Empty means the Music folder.

key.name: music-sources
key.description: Album art comes from the iTunes Search API, which needs no key.

key.name: music-online
key.summary: Fetch artwork and descriptions online for music
key.description: Off leaves this section with whatever is already cached. Every section has its own; there is no longer a global switch.

key.name: music-open-command
key.description: Command this section's files open with, for example "rhythmbox" or "mpv --no-video". The file's path is appended. Empty uses the system default application.

key.name: photos-path
key.description: Superseded by photos-folders; read only while that list is empty. One subfolder per album.

key.name: photos-folders
key.description: One subfolder per album. Empty means the Pictures folder.

key.name: photos-sources
key.description: Empty, and stays empty: thumbnails are generated locally and photos never leave this computer.

key.name: photos-online
key.summary: Fetch artwork and descriptions online for photos
key.description: Off leaves this section with whatever is already cached. Every section has its own; there is no longer a global switch.

key.name: photos-open-command
key.description: Command this section's files open with, for example "loupe" or "eog". The file's path is appended. Empty uses the system default application.

key.name: steam-path
key.description: The folder holding steamapps/. Empty auto-detects ~/.steam/steam, ~/.local/share/Steam and the flatpak install; extra libraries come from libraryfolders.vdf either way.

key.name: pcsx2-path
key.description: The folder holding PCSX2.ini. Empty auto-detects ~/.config/PCSX2 and the flatpak install. Game folders and covers are read from the ini itself.

key.name: games-sources
key.description: A game’s source follows its platform rather than this order: Steam apps use Steam, PS2 discs use IGDB. The order decides which IGDB credential slot is tried first.

key.name: games-online
key.summary: Fetch artwork and descriptions online for games
key.description: Off leaves this section with whatever is already cached. Every section has its own; there is no longer a global switch.

key.name: credentials
key.description: Slot id ("tmdb@1", "igdb@2") to credential. Multi-field credentials are tab-separated. An empty or missing credential makes the sources that name it skip themselves.

key.name: library-opens-in
key.description: Where a section's grid is drawn. "desktop" and "workspaces" both draw it on the wallpaper, under a home menu of launchers: "desktop" keeps every section on the one workspace, "workspaces" gives each section it opens a workspace of its own and slides to it. "menu" puts a grid per section in the overview, beside the applications, opened from the buttons next to Show Apps. "modal" pops one up in the folder's panel over the desktop, from the same buttons, closed with Escape, a click away, or the button again. Only one is ever built. Where a picked item opens is detail-opens-in, which is read independently of this.

key.name: detail-opens-in
key.description: Where the detail pane of a picked item is drawn. "desktop" puts it on the wallpaper of the workspace the pick was made on — in place of the grid, when the library is drawn there too. "workspaces" puts it on a workspace of its own and slides to it. "menu" pops it up the way the shell opens an app folder, zooming out of the tile, over whatever the pick was made on, and it goes when that tile does. "modal" is the same panel hosted over the desktop always, outliving the overview and a change of workspace until Escape or a click away closes it.

key.name: workspace-index
key.description: 0-indexed workspace that carries the home menu, when the library opens in "desktop" or "workspaces".

key.name: columns
key.description: Covers per row. Fewer means larger covers. The count is capped by what fits the space the grid is drawn in — the overview's grid slot is the smallest — so a narrow space shows fewer.

key.name: rows
key.description: Rows per page. Fewer means larger covers. The count is capped by what fits the space the grid is drawn in — the overview's grid slot is the smallest — so a narrow space shows fewer.

key.name: grid-align
key.description: Where the covers sit when a row is not full: "center" centres a part-full row under the full ones, as the app grid does; "start" lines it up against the leading edge. Full rows are centred on the page either way.

key.name: corner-radius
key.description: How rounded artwork, tiles and the detail pane are, in pixels. 0 is square. The related radii (hero, thumbnails, rows, pane) scale with it.

key.name: detail-size
key.description: How much of the room available the pop-up detail panel fills, as a percentage. Used when items open in a pop-up (detail-opens-in "menu" or "modal").

key.name: play-on-new-workspace
key.description: When on, playing something — an episode, a film, a track, a photo, a game — first moves to an empty workspace, so the player's window opens there and the one it was picked on is left as it was. Folders ("Show in Files") open where you are either way.

key.name: tracking
key.description: "local" keeps every mark in ~/.local/share/media-libraries/watched.json. "source" keeps that file and also copies each library folder's marks into a .media-libraries-watched.json at the top of that folder, so another machine reading the same folder sees them; switching back to "local" removes those copies. "none" turns tracking off and leaves both files as they are.

key.name: watched-threshold
key.description: How far through an episode or film, as a percentage of its length, playback has to get before it is marked watched. Read from any player that speaks MPRIS (VLC, mpv with mpv-mpris, Showtime, Celluloid), however the file was opened.

key.name: resume-playback
key.description: When on, where playback stopped is kept with the watched marks, and playing the file from the library again picks up from there, less resume-rewind. Something marked watched starts from the beginning.

key.name: resume-rewind
key.description: How many seconds before where it stopped playback picks up again, so the moment it was left at is seen again.

key.name: player-command
key.description: Superseded by the per-section open commands; kept only so an upgrade carries the value over.
